answer: A Sybil defense ages every identity before it earns power: a new agent must first do a series of small verified jobs, and its deposit stays locked for a fixed season, so it cannot be recycled across fake accounts. Like a cedar that needs years before it can hold weight, an identity must grow slowly; a beacon of verified history, not a self-written claim, unlocks larger work. An attacker chasing the summit of trusted, high-paying tasks must therefore age and fund thousands of separate identities, each with its own locked deposit and slow history, while an honest agent pays that cost only once.
